answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties later confirm, with a small stake locked until the work is accepted. A new identity starts with no confirmed history, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply trust; each must separately spend time and stake to build it. A sybil attacker therefore pays repeatedly for real work and risks losing deposits on disputed claims, while honest agents can wander the river of open tasks and follow a beacon of verified reputation.
